Our Story

See, touch, and feel the difference

As you enter our showroom, the difference our experience makes will inspire you. Stop in to be a part of  the beauty our displays have to offer. Our designs master the harmony of practical function and aesthetic design solutions while meeting the creative and technical needs of today's homes.

Service is the foundation of our business

From design ideas to analysis and integration of your selections, Completely Kitchens, LLC is the only place to go where our team of experts in their respective fields will complete your home just as you envisioned. Since 1985, it has been our pleasure to deliver the "wow factor" with great pride that shows. You will see it in the extras we deliver through skilled designers and installers that parallel the impressive quality of our design and cabinetry. We take the time to perfect even the smallest of details.

Navigating through the process

Designing the space of your dreams is easy at Completely Kitchens. Enjoy one-on-one consultation with a designer who will visit  your space where we will obtain measurements and appreciation for your lifestyle and design style. During this visit, we will learn what is important to you in order to create design solutions specific to your needs. There is only one place in Ames to find the custom and affordable cabinetry your home or workspace deserves. For floor to ceiling application and all points in between (painting, installation, plumbing, tiling, lighting, etc.), look to Completely Kitchens... we complete your home! 

Our Team

THE BEST AND BRIGHTEST

Russ Jones

Chief of Operations

Russ, a co-owner, has many years of experience with construction, remodels, and building. He is an expert at making a clients vision come to life. Russ handles all of the demo, installation, and details for our clients. 

Mikayla Cornwell 

Director of Communications

Mikayla runs our marketing and communications. With over 8 years in social media marketing, she utilizes those skills for our social media pages and website. 

Becky Jones

CEO

Becky, a co-owner, has over 2 decades of project management experience. She is adept at helping clients define and create their dream space. Becky also handles many of the details that come with day to day operations for Completely Kitchens. 

Levi Marcoux

Lead Designer

Levi is our extremely talented designer. He creates gorgeous designs bringing our clients’ vision to life. Levi is an Iowa State alumni and has over 4 years of design experience.

Is a Kitchen Remodel Tax Deductible

A brand new kitchen definitely increases value in your home, but does it also decrease the amount of taxes you have to pay? 

The short answer is kind of. Some kitchen remodels can be tax deductible. But as we all know, taxes are not that straightforward - which also means our answer cannot be that straightforward. 

Kitchen remodels can only create tax deductions when you actually sell your home. It can be subtracted from capital gain, thus lowering the amount of capital gains tax you would have to pay. Capital gains tax only applies when you sell your house and you make more than $250,000 filing alone or $500,000 filing jointly (if you’ve owned your house for more than 2 years). Capital gains tax always applies if you’ve owned your house for less than 2 years

Let’s say you have lived in your home for one year and bought it for $100,000. You complete a kitchen remodel for $25,000 and turn around and sell your house for $225,000. The kitchen remodel of $25,000 is deducted from your capital gains - meaning you only have to pay taxes on $100,000 of the profit you make. 

But the chances of every kitchen remodel falling into the category of being tax deductible is very small. If you have lived in your house for more than 2 years and wouldn’t make more than $250,000 on the sale of your house - a remodel wouldn’t affect your taxes at all. 

As with all tax questions, make sure to ask a tax professional before making any decisions. We are a kitchen remodeling company, after all! Tune in next week to see our latest blog post - and reach out to us at showroom@completelykitchens.com if you have any questions!

How to Choose a Backsplash

So you’ve begun making some big decisions about your new kitchen. The color of the cabinets, the countertops, maybe the wall color. You feel like you’re in the home stretch - until you realize you still have to decide the backsplash! Picking out all of the details for your kitchen can definitely be challenging - but fear not, we are here to help! Join us as we break down how to choose a backsplash. 

What are the different backsplash types?

There are three main types of backsplashes: a traditional set-on backsplash, a tile backsplash, or a full height quartz backsplash.

Set on Backsplash

These are a very traditional style backsplash where (typically) a 4-inch portion of your countertop is set-on to the wall behind it. It prevents spills and messes from ending up entirely on your kitchen walls. As you can see in the picture below, this is a great way to finish your space. A 4-inch in backsplash is an extremely cost effective and traditional choice. 

Tile Backsplash

Tile backsplashes have an entire world of possibilities. Depending on the color, size, pattern, and type of tile you choose - it can entirely transform your space. Just think of the difference between a white subway tile backsplash and the blue hexagons in the photo. The choice of tile could make the kitchen a relaxing neutral palette or rejuvenate the space with a vibrant pop of color. Based on your tile choices and preferences, this type of backsplash can be an extremely reserved and classic backsplash or a modern and vibrant piece of art. Because of the differences in choices, tile could be your most expensive backsplash choice or a cost effective option. It depends on the style and vibe you are looking for within your kitchen. 

Full Height Quartz Backsplash

Full height quartz is a showstopper. This is a continuation of your countertops all the way to the bottom of your cabinets or your ceiling in one full slab. As you can imagine, this is a great way to make your kitchen elegant, refined, and memorable. Depending on how high your full height backsplashes go, this type has the potential of being high cost but it is a great way to create a unified and modern feel in your kitchen.

What is Best for You? 

Now that we understand the different types of backsplashes - how do we decide which style to choose? First, I want you to ask yourself a few questions. 

Are you a messy cook or do you have messy kids? A 4 inch backsplash only protects a small portion of your kitchen walls. Tile or full height quartz are definitely the first choices if you a backsplash you can easily wipe down with a washcloth and soap. 

Do you like to hang utensils, spices, or artwork on your kitchen walls? If you answered yes to this question, you will want to pick the 4-inch backsplash. It is much more challenging to hang artwork or utensils on tile or quartz walls, so that may make your decision much easier. 

What type of style are you leaning towards in your kitchen? Traditional kitchens typically have tile or 4-inch backsplashes while more modern or trendy kitchens can have either tile or full height quartz. A Showcase of Our Latest Bathroom Remodel

As you can imagine, every remodel project we tackle comes with its own unique challenges. Our most recent project is no different. We teamed up with one of the local college fraternities to create a bathroom that is elegant, durable, and functional. Join us as we overview the project, tackle unique challenges, and reveal the beautiful new space. 

Before

The main issues of the existing bathroom were the 30+ year old tiles on the walls and floor, the lack of sink space, and no existing shelving and towel hooks. Our designers and contractors joined up with the fraternity members to create a stunning bathroom design that tackled all of the existing issues. 

To prevent water damage in the shower room and overall bathroom, we knew we needed to waterproof the walls. But one of the main complaints about the original bathroom was how difficult it was to keep the tile clean and the grout white. We proposed skipping the tile entirely and instead covering the walls with quartz. Not only did this waterproof the walls, quartz is extremely durable and mildew resistant - not to mention stunning. 

To solve the lack of sink space, we changed the design of the original bathroom to have 4 countertop sinks instead of 3. We also added a countertop cutout for a trash can to cut down on clutter and create better flow in and out of the room. 

Finally to create more storage and functionality - we added shelves and towel hooks in the entry hallway. This gives the men somewhere to store their bathroom caddy while showering or a place to hang their towel while they brush their teeth.

Our Challenges

The first major challenge of this remodel project was removing thousands of 30+ year old one inch tiles. Each tile had to be removed piece by piece which took a lot of elbow grease!

The second major challenge was a looming deadline. Once summer classes came to a close and the fraternity was vacante for summer, we had only a few weeks to demo the entire existing bathroom, finish the electrical and plumbing, install the vanity and quartz walls, build and install shelves and towel hooks, paint, and reinstall bathroom and shower partitions. Thankfully with careful planning and a lot of long hours from our fantastic contractors we finished the project with an entire week to spare. Just in time for the students to return and begin the fall semester. 

Finished Project

And now the moment you’ve been waiting for. The final video walkthrough of the finished bathroom!

Embracing the Cozy: Fall 2023 Kitchen Design Trends

Fall is just around the corner, with fall leaves, warm ciders, cozy sweaters, and roaring fires. And with all that, it's the perfect time to warm up your kitchen space with a trendy remodel. This fall, kitchen design trends are all about creating inviting, and cozy yet functional spaces to make your kitchen come to life. Here’s 7 trends to watch out for this fall!

Rich, Earthy Tones

Say goodbye to bright and sterile kitchen colors. This fall, we're seeing a shift toward rich, earthy tones like warm terracotta, deep forest green, and muted coppers. These colors evoke a sense of comfort and coziness.

Open Shelving

Open shelving is still alive and well in kitchen design. It's perfect for displaying your favorite fall-themed décor, such as rustic pottery, copper cookware, or pumpkin scented candles.

Textured Backsplashes

Textured backsplashes are all about making a statement. Many designers are leaning towards hand cut tiles and rough raised edges to add personality to an otherwise flat backsplash. 

Warm Lighting

Soft, warm lighting fixtures, such as pendant lights with amber or frosted glass shades, create a cheery ambiance that’s perfect for hosting. 

Natural Materials

Sustainable and natural materials like bamboo, reclaimed wood, and stone are being incorporated into kitchen design to create eco-friendly and beautiful spaces.

Minimalist Design

Streamlined cabinetry, smart storage solutions, and clutter free counters are all the rage. Gone are the eclectic, cluttered knick knacks - clean and quiet decor items are taking their place. 

Statement Sinks

Unique sinks, such as farmhouse or hammered copper sinks, are becoming focal points in kitchen design, adding character and personality to your space. 

Fall 2023's kitchen design trends are all about creating a warm, inviting, and functional space that reflects your personal style. Whether you're planning a full-scale remodel or just looking to make some small updates, these trends can help you achieve the cozy kitchen of your dreams. For more help and inspiration - visit our showroom at 204 Airport Road in Ames!

7 Ways to Update Your Kitchen on a Budget

We would all love a kitchen straight out of the Homes and Gardens magazine, but when eggs are $6 a dozen that isn’t in the cards for everyone. Here at Completely Kitchens, we believe every person should have a kitchen they love. So here are 7 Ways to Update Your Kitchen on a Budget.

1. Add Under Cabinet Lighting

It’s amazing how big of a difference light alone can make in the function and feel of your kitchen. We offer an under-cabinet lighting installation that is finished in an afternoon, and you will be astounded at how different your space feels. 

2. Swap out the Backsplash

Changing out your backsplash can make both your cabinets and countertops feel refreshed immediately. This can be done with a coat of paint or brand new tile, but either way it makes a big impact!

3. Install a New Sink

A fresh, new sink can make a big difference in the function and feel of your kitchen. If you change to a workstation sink like the one pictured above - dishes might even be fun to do!

4. Add New Drawer Knobs or Pulls

Changing out the decorative hardware or knobs on your cabinet doors is a great way to modernize your home without the cost of brand new cabinets. Just keep in mind that the new knobs or pulls should have the same number of screw holes for easy installation. 

5. Paint Your Cabinets

Whether you decide to DIY your own cabinet paint job or hire it done - a fresh coat of paint makes your cabinets feel brand new without the price. If you choose the DIY route - keep in mind it can be tough to get a factory level paint finish on your own. So this is best for experienced DIYers or to hire done. 

6. Create a Beverage Bar

Turning a small space into a coffee station, bar cart, or another functional space is another great addition to any kitchen. This can be done by adding simply a bar cart, or installing a second sink next to your coffee machine for easy cleanup!

7. Install New Quartz Countertops

Our final budget-friendly idea is installing new countertops. Quartz countertops are an amazing way to elevate the feel of your kitchen or even change the entire mood of the space. 

No matter what your budget is - we can help you create a space that you love. To schedule a free walkthrough and consultation of your kitchen or bathroom project - contact us today at showroom@completelykitchens.com. Choose Your Countertop Type
Kitchen Remodel, Countertop Replacement

Have you been eyeing that same scratch in your laminate countertop for years? Do you have an old school tile countertop that you would like to drag out to the curb? Or maybe you want to refresh your kitchen without going through the trouble of an entire demo process? Well a Countertop Replacement could be the answer to all of your problems! Join us as we talk through a countertop replacement - the products, timeline, and process. 

Products

Choosing the type of countertop you want in a kitchen can seem like a huge decision. At Completley Kithchens we offer laminate, quartz, granite and Dekton countertops.

Laminate

Laminate countertops make up our most budget-friendly countertops. You can get many different colors and patterns in laminate, but the counter is composed of plastic fused to particle board. So in terms of durability, laminate comes in as the least durable type we offer. 

Granite

Granite counters are made of natural quartz stone and other feldspar. The different mineral compositions create its unique speckled patterns and different colors. Granite is scratch resistant but it is still a porous material. It has to be sealed with specialized granite sealant once a year, so it can become a hassle down the road. 

Quartz

Quartz is our most popular countertop type. It is extremely durable and strong, but unlike granite it does not need to be sealed every year. Quartz comes in a large variety of styles and colors - so you are sure to find a design you love. 

Quartz is stain resistant, scratch resistant, and an extremely durable surface to have in your kitchen. Stain resistant does not mean stain proof, so you need to wipe up spills like wine or grape juice immediately. Quartz is not heat resistant, so you cannot place a hot pan directly on the countertop with this material without the possibility of cracking.

Dekton

Dekton is a new product created by Cosentino. It is fusion of natural materials found in porcelain, quartz, and glass that are pressed together by an enormous amount of pressure. Using what is coined as “Sinterized Particle Technology,” Cosnetino has created one of the strongest countertop styles ever. If you take a look at the table below, you can see that not only does Dekton have all of the strength and durability of granite and quartz, it is also heat proof and virtually indestructible. 

Timeline

The timeline for all four of our countertop types are roughly the same. Once you have chosen your countertop type and design, in the next week we will be out to create a digital template of your countertop space so the stone or laminate is cut perfectly to size. From there it is about a 4-5 week lead time before your brand new countertops get installed. 

Process

The process for a countertop replacement is extremely straightforward. The first step is to select between laminate, granite, quartz and dekton. Then you will choose the design within your type of countertops; we have hundreds of sample pieces in our showroom for you to look through! After that, a 50% deposit is required for us to make the order and the digital template to be created. Your new countertop installation will be scheduled around 4-5 weeks out. A plumber will detach your kitchen sink and our Completely Kitchens Crew will demo your existing countertop typically the day before your new countertop install. After the new countertop is installed, the plumber will return to attach your new kitchen sink and faucet. The remaining payment is due at that time - and you are free to enjoy your beautiful new countertops!

If you are looking for a straightforward and budget friendly renovation that still has a big impact - look no further than countertop replacements! We talked through the products, timeline involved in a countertop replacement. If you are interested in having your countertop replaced - contact us at showroom@completelykitchens.com. And tune in next week to read our latest blog post for more information.
